300 small mental health tips you can try today

Every tip here is one small, specific thing to do, not a lifestyle to adopt. They are the 300 tips Theraglee members see one a day, sorted by what they help with.

Free to read. Create a free account to get one a day on your dashboard, picked for what matters to you.

How to use this page

Do not try to do many. Read the section for the thing that is loudest this week and pick one tip you could do in the next hour. Try it for a few days. If it helps, keep it; if it does not, pick another. Small and repeated beats large and abandoned.

None of these tips treat or cure anything. They are the kind of thing a steady friend might suggest. If what you are dealing with is bigger than a tip, that is what a licensed therapist is for.

Sleep tips

  • Pick a wake-up time and keep it tomorrow, weekend or not.
  • Dim the lights at home an hour before bed tonight.
  • Keep your bedroom a little cool tonight, around 65 to 68 degrees.
  • Charge your phone outside the bedroom tonight. A cheap alarm clock does the job.
  • Have your last coffee by 2pm today. Caffeine lingers longer than it feels like it does.
  • Write tomorrow's to-do list before bed so your brain doesn't rehearse it at 2am.
  • Save your bed for sleep. Scroll, work, and worry somewhere else.
  • Take a warm shower an hour or two before bed. The cool-down afterward nudges sleepiness.
  • If you nap today, keep it under 30 minutes and before 3pm.
  • Read a paper book for 15 minutes in bed instead of a screen.
  • Set a wind-down alarm for 45 minutes before bedtime.
  • Finish heavy meals two to three hours before bed tonight.
  • If you wake at 3am, don't check the time. Clock-watching feeds the alertness.
  • Block the light at your bedroom window tonight, even with a towel over the gap.
  • Go to bed when you're sleepy, not just when the clock says so.
  • Log two numbers each morning this week: bedtime and wake time. Patterns show up fast.
  • Try a body scan in bed: notice your toes, then feet, then ankles, all the way up.
  • Skip the nightcap tonight. Alcohol makes the second half of the night's sleep lighter.
  • Before bed, list three things that went well and one you're letting go of.
  • After sunset, turn your screen brightness down to match the room.
  • Do your evening routine in the same order tonight. Repetition tells your body sleep is coming.
  • After a bad night, keep your usual wake time anyway. It helps tomorrow night.

Anxiety tips

  • Exhale longer than you inhale for two minutes: in for 4, out for 6.
  • Before a nerve-racking call, write your first sentence on a sticky note.
  • When your chest tightens, press your feet into the floor and count five slow breaths.
  • Ask of one fear today: what's the most likely outcome, not the worst one?
  • Hold a cold glass of water in both hands and notice the temperature for 30 seconds.
  • Do one small thing you've avoided out of nerves. Notice the dread was bigger than the task.
  • Rate your anxiety 0 to 10 now and again in 20 minutes. Feelings crest and fall on their own.
  • Write what you'd actually do if the thing you fear happened. A plan shrinks the fear.
  • Replace "what if" with "even if" once today, then finish the sentence.
  • Relax your jaw, drop your shoulders, and unclench your hands. Check again at lunch.
  • Arrive ten minutes early to one thing today so your nervous system isn't sprinting.
  • When your heart races, name it plainly: this is adrenaline, and it passes.
  • Hum one low note for a full exhale. The vibration helps slow your breathing.
  • Skip one reassurance check today. Sit with the not-knowing for five minutes.
  • Keep a "predicted vs. actual" note: what you feared, then later what really happened.
  • Walk briskly for 12 minutes when anxiety spikes. Give the energy somewhere to go.
  • Put a hand on your chest and breathe so it rises under your palm, six times.
  • Take one slow breath at every red light or doorway today.
  • Swap one catastrophic word for an accurate one: "awful" becomes "uncomfortable."
  • Keep a small comfort object in your bag for anxious moments.

Relationships tips

  • Ask someone close, "What was the best part of your day?" and really listen.
  • Put your phone face down during one meal with someone today.
  • Thank your partner, friend, or roommate for one specific thing they did this week.
  • In a disagreement, repeat back what you heard before you respond.
  • Try "I feel ___ when ___" once today instead of "you always."
  • Turn toward one small bid for attention today: look up, answer, smile.
  • Set a standing catch-up with someone you miss, same day each month.
  • Apologize for one small thing without adding "but."
  • When someone's message reads as curt, assume good intent once and see what happens.
  • Ask a friend how you can support them this week, then do exactly that.
  • In a heated argument, take a 20-minute break and say when you'll come back.
  • Notice one thing someone does well and tell them within the hour.
  • Hug someone you trust for a full 20 seconds today.
  • Send a family member a one-line check-in with no agenda.
  • Ask one follow-up question today instead of jumping to your own story.
  • Plan one shared activity this week that doesn't involve a screen.
  • Stop keeping score for a day. Do one kind thing without tracking who owes whom.
  • Plan a phone call with a friend this week and put it on both calendars.
  • Tell someone what they mean to you, in one sentence, while they can hear it.
  • Share one small worry with a friend today and let them help carry it.

Self compassion tips

  • Put a hand on your arm and say, "This is hard, and I'm doing my best."
  • Write yourself a two-line note from the point of view of a kind friend.
  • When you make a mistake today, say "of course" instead of calling yourself names.
  • Swap one "should" for "could" today. Notice what shifts.
  • Use your own name in self-talk today, like a coach: "Okay, one step at a time."
  • List three things you'd forgive a friend for that you still hold against yourself.
  • Rest without earning it. Sit down for 10 minutes before the chores are done.
  • Listen to the tone of your inner voice today. Would you hire it as a coach?
  • Thank your body for one thing it did today, like carrying you up the stairs.
  • When the inner critic starts, answer it with one fact about your effort.
  • Let yourself be a beginner at something today, clumsy and all.
  • Treat a setback like a weather report: note it, dress for it, keep going.
  • Write down one thing you're proud of handling this month.
  • Forgive yourself for one small thing from this week, out loud.
  • Say one sentence of encouragement to yourself in the mirror this morning.
  • Keep a folder of kind messages people have sent you. Open it on rough days.
  • Write yourself a permission slip for one evening off.
  • When a harsh thought about your body shows up, name one thing it lets you do.
  • Recall someone who was kind to you when you struggled. Offer yourself the same.
  • Say one kind thing to yourself before you get out of bed.

Depression tips

  • Do one thing for five minutes that used to bring you joy, even if it doesn't feel fun yet.
  • Act first, feel later: take the shower before deciding if you're up to it.
  • Open the curtains as soon as you're up.
  • Rate your mood 1 to 10 before and after a short walk. Let the data argue with the gloom.
  • Put away five things and count it as a real win.
  • Eat something at a regular mealtime today, even if you're not hungry.
  • Get dressed in real clothes today, even if you're staying home.
  • Tell one trusted person, "I'm having a heavy day." You don't need to explain more.
  • When your mind says "nothing will help," treat it as a symptom talking, not a fact.
  • Plan tomorrow with one pleasant thing and one useful thing, each 10 minutes long.
  • Sit by a window for 15 minutes this morning with your coffee or tea.
  • Brush your teeth even on a hard day. Small care is still care.
  • Write down three things you did today, however small. Getting up counts.
  • Ask someone to come along on a short errand. Company makes it easier to go.
  • If you've felt low most days for two weeks, book a check-in with a doctor or therapist.
  • Put on music with a beat while you do one chore.
  • Schedule one pleasant activity for your lowest time of day.
  • Step outside for fresh air today, even for two minutes.
  • When a thought says "always" or "never," find one exception.

Stress tips

  • Drop your shoulders away from your ears right now. Stress tends to live two inches too high.
  • Pick one obligation this week to cancel, postpone, or hand off. Do it today.
  • Take a five-minute walk without your phone between two tasks.
  • Sigh on purpose: two short inhales through the nose, one long exhale through the mouth. Three times.
  • Write down the three things stressing you most, then circle the one you control.
  • Eat lunch away from your desk today, even if it's only 15 minutes.
  • Tense your fists for five seconds, then let go. Work up from hands to shoulders.
  • Put a 10-minute buffer between meetings in today's calendar.
  • Put on one song you love and do nothing else for its length.
  • Before replying to a stressful email, stand up and get a drink of water.
  • Say "this is a stressful moment" to yourself. Naming it gives you a half-step of room.
  • Clear one flat surface at home. A small patch of order calms a busy head.
  • Stretch your neck slowly side to side for one minute at 3pm.
  • Lower one standard today. Store-bought is fine, and so is a shorter email.
  • Spend 10 minutes near trees or plants today. A park bench counts.
  • During your next stressful task, check your breath. If you're holding it, let it out.
  • Before a busy week, write down the one thing you'll protect no matter what.
  • Use shoulder tension as your cue to get up and refill your water.

Habits tips

  • Attach a new habit to an old one: after I pour coffee, I'll stretch for one minute.
  • Set your walking shoes by the door tonight.
  • Make one bad habit a step harder, like logging out of the app after each use.
  • Shrink a habit to its two-minute version: one push-up, one page, one line.
  • Write the when and where of one new habit: "At 7pm, in the kitchen, I will..."
  • If you skip a habit, pick it up the next day without a lecture.
  • Leave a book on your pillow so it's waiting at bedtime.
  • Put your gym bag in the car tonight.
  • Remove one cue for a habit you want to drop, like snacks on the counter.
  • Ask what one habit does for you, then find a gentler way to get that.
  • Set your phone to grayscale for one afternoon and see how often you reach for it.
  • On Sunday, review one habit: keep it, shrink it, or swap it.
  • Pick one habit to do at the same time every day this week.

Boundaries tips

  • Practice saying "Let me check and get back to you" instead of an instant yes.
  • Turn off work notifications at a set time tonight.
  • Say no to one small request today, kindly and briefly.
  • Decide in advance how long you'll stay at an event, and leave then.
  • Notice resentment today. It often marks a boundary you haven't set yet.
  • Mute one busy group chat for eight hours.
  • Let one call go to voicemail and return it when you have the energy.
  • Write down three values and drop one commitment that fits none of them.

Burnout tips

  • Protect one evening this week from anything work-related.
  • If work feels pointless lately, read it as a sign to rest, not to push harder.
  • Ask for one deadline to move this week, calmly and early.
  • Take your full lunch break today and leave the building for part of it.
  • List what drains you and what refills you this week. Swap one drain for a refill.
  • Do something today that's purely for you and produces nothing.
  • Use a vacation day before you're forced to take one.
  • When resentment shows up at work, check what you've overcommitted to.

Procrastination tips

  • Open the file you're avoiding and write a bad first sentence. That's the whole job for now.
  • Tell someone when you'll finish a task and ask them to check in.
  • Work alongside someone else for an hour, in person or on video.
  • Leave tomorrow's first task open on your desk tonight.
  • Name the feeling you're avoiding, not the task. Then start.
  • Pair a dull task with a podcast you only allow yourself during it.
  • Forgive yesterday's procrastination. Guilt tends to fuel more delay.
  • Keep a list of five easy first steps for days you feel stuck.

Grief tips

  • Say the name of someone you've lost out loud today, in a sentence you enjoy.
  • Set aside 15 minutes for a memory of someone you miss: a photo, a song, a recipe.
  • Let grief come in waves today. You don't have to feel all of it at once.
  • Write a short letter to someone you've lost. It doesn't need to be sent anywhere.
  • Mark hard anniversaries on your calendar ahead of time and plan something gentle.
  • Tell someone a story about the person you miss. Grief often wants a witness.
  • Name one small loss you haven't grieved yet: a job, a place, a plan.

Mindfulness tips

  • Take your first sip of coffee or tea slowly, noticing its warmth and smell.
  • Eat the first three bites of lunch without a screen.
  • Wash one dish slowly and notice the water, the weight, and the sound.
  • Listen for the farthest sound you can hear for one minute.
  • Watch one thought pass today like a car on the street, without following it.
  • Take one breath before you open any app today.
  • Walk the last 100 feet to your door noticing each step.

Trauma tips

  • When you feel on edge, find five blue things in the room. It pulls attention to now.
  • Notice what helps you feel safe, like a blanket, a song, or a scent. Keep one close.
  • Say to yourself, "That was then. This is now." Then name today's date.
  • Give yourself permission to step out of a room that feels like too much.
  • Set your own pace. You don't owe anyone your story on their schedule.
  • Write down three signs your body gives when it feels calm, so you can spot them.
  • If old memories keep intruding, look for a therapist trained in trauma care.

Anger tips

  • When anger flares, wait 90 seconds before speaking. Let the first surge pass.
  • Walk fast around the block before responding to something that made you angry.
  • Write the angry message in a notes app, not the reply box. Reread it tomorrow.
  • Look for the hurt underneath the anger and name it.
  • Lower your voice and open your hands on purpose. The body can lead the mood down.
  • Splash cool water on your face when anger runs hot.

Confidence tips

  • Do one thing today before you feel ready. Readiness often shows up after starting.
  • Rehearse a hard conversation out loud once, in the car or the shower.
  • Stand tall and take three slow breaths before you walk into a room.
  • Recall a time you handled something hard. Write down the one skill you used.
  • Speak up once in a meeting today, even if it's only a question.
  • Delete one "just" or "sorry" from an email before you send it.

Emotions tips

  • Get more precise: instead of "bad," try "disappointed," "lonely," or "on edge."
  • Ask what an emotion wants: rest, reassurance, action, or space?
  • Let yourself cry if it comes. Tears are one way feelings move through.
  • Write for five minutes about a feeling, then close the notebook.
  • Rate an emotion's strength from 1 to 10 before you act on it.
  • Check the facts: does this emotion fit the situation, and does it fit its size?

Gratitude tips

  • Write three good things from today and why each one happened.
  • Thank someone whose work usually goes unnoticed, like a mail carrier or custodian.
  • At dinner, name one thing that went better than expected.
  • Name one ordinary thing you'd miss if it vanished, like hot water.
  • Write a thank-you note to a teacher or mentor who helped you.
  • Take a photo of one small good thing today.

Hope tips

  • Write down one thing you're looking forward to next month.
  • Picture yourself six months from now, doing a little better. What first step did they take?
  • Read about someone who came through something like what you're facing.
  • Plant something, even basil in a cup. Tending it is a small act of hope.
  • Say "not yet" instead of "never" about one goal today.
  • Write down one thing that got better this year.

Mood tips

  • Stand in sunlight for five minutes around midday.
  • Check what you've eaten and drunk today before blaming yourself for a bad mood.
  • Note your mood at noon and 8pm for three days. Look for what moves it.
  • Call instead of texting today. A voice lifts mood more than typed words.
  • Tidy for exactly 10 minutes with a timer, then stop.
  • Do something kind for a stranger today without telling anyone.

Perfectionism tips

  • Hand something in today at "good enough" and watch nothing collapse.
  • Give a task a time cap, and stop when it ends, finished or not.
  • Leave one tiny thing imperfect on purpose, like a crooked picture. Notice you're fine.
  • Before another round of edits, ask who would notice the difference. If no one, stop.
  • Celebrate a finished draft today, not a perfect one.
  • Let someone load the dishwasher their way today, and leave it.

Self care tips

  • Change your sheets today. Clean sheets count as self-care.
  • Book the appointment you keep putting off: dentist, doctor, or haircut.
  • Put lotion on your hands slowly, as if it matters. It does.
  • List five low-effort things that comfort you and stick it on the fridge.
  • Pack tomorrow's lunch tonight.
  • Refill your water bottle each time you finish a task.

Worry tips

  • Sort today's worries into two columns: can act on, can't act on. Act on one.
  • When a worry shows up after 9pm, jot it on a notepad by the bed and let paper hold it.
  • Ask of one worry: will this matter in five days, five months, or five years?
  • Turn one worry into a question you can answer with a single next step.
  • Give a recurring worry a silly nickname. The fifth rerun is harder to take seriously.
  • Check the news once today, at a set time, and close the app after.

Change tips

  • Keep one routine steady during a big change, like your morning coffee spot.
  • List what's staying the same during a change you're going through.
  • Try one tiny change this week, like a new route for your walk.
  • Give a new situation 30 days before you judge it. Write the date down.
  • Talk to someone who's made the change you're considering.

Loneliness tips

  • Work from a café or library for an hour. Being around people counts.
  • Sign up for one recurring class or group, even if it starts next month.
  • Offer to help someone with a small task this week. Helping builds connection.
  • Reply to one message you've been leaving on read.
  • Walk at the same time each day this week. Familiar faces start to nod back.

Overwhelm tips

  • Empty everything on your mind onto one page, then cross off what isn't yours to carry.
  • Do the next small visible thing. Not the whole list, just that.
  • Set a timer for 20 minutes, work, and stop. Then decide what's next.
  • Turn off nonessential notifications for the rest of the day.
  • Ask for help with one piece of the pile, and be specific about which.

Resilience tips

  • List three people you could call on a bad night. Save them as favorites in your phone.
  • Ask what one thing today's setback can teach you.
  • Pack a small tough-day kit: a snack, a playlist, a comfort show.
  • Finish the sentence "I got through..." three different ways.
  • When plans fall apart, pick the next good-enough step, not the perfect one.

Rest tips

  • Lie down for 10 minutes with your eyes closed and no phone.
  • Take a real break: step away from screens, not just to a different one.
  • Keep Saturday morning free of plans until 11am.
  • Lie on the floor with your legs up the wall for five minutes this evening.
  • Leave five minutes between tasks to reset, stretch, or refill your tea.

Work tips

  • Start your workday with the hardest 25 minutes, before email.
  • Check email at three set times today, not all day.
  • Close every browser tab you don't need for the next hour.
  • Stand and walk for two minutes each hour at your desk.
  • Write the one outcome that would make today's work a good day.

Acceptance tips

  • Use "and" instead of "but": "I'm anxious, and I'm going anyway."
  • Let one thing you can't change sit for five minutes without arguing with it.
  • Write "This is how it is, and here's what I'll do" about one problem.
  • Notice a feeling you dislike and tell yourself, "I can make room for this."

Body tips

  • Roll your shoulders back five times, then stretch your arms overhead.
  • Every 20 minutes of screen time, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
  • Take the stairs once today at a pace that feels good.
  • Find where you're holding tension right now and let that spot soften on the exhale.

Focus tips

  • Work one 25-minute block with your phone in another room.
  • Keep a "later" pad by you. Write down distractions and get back to the task.
  • Choose one task as today's must-do. Everything else is a bonus.
  • Pick one playlist as your cue to focus and play it only while you work.

Motivation tips

  • Write why one goal matters to you in a single sentence and tape it where you'll see it.
  • Don't wait to feel motivated. Start for five minutes and let motivation catch up.
  • Give yourself a small reward right after finishing one hard thing today.
  • Break a goal into steps small enough that you can finish one today.

Communication tips

  • Say what you need in one sentence before you give the backstory.
  • Pause for two seconds before answering someone today.
  • End a hard conversation by agreeing on one next step.

Connection tips

  • Say hello to a neighbor or cashier by name, or ask theirs.
  • Send an old friend a photo with "This reminded me of you."
  • Join one conversation today that you'd usually just listen to.

Courage tips

  • Ask the question you think makes you look silly. Others probably wondered too.
  • Do one thing today that scares you a little and is perfectly safe.
  • Share an honest opinion once today, calmly.

Grounding tips

  • Hold something textured, like a key or a stone, and describe it to yourself.
  • Count backward from 100 by sevens when your mind races.
  • Sit with your back against a wall and feel it hold you up for one minute.

Healing tips

  • Notice one way you're gentler with yourself than you were two years ago.
  • Write down one sign of progress, then reread it on a rough day. Healing isn't a straight line.
  • Try one new way of coping for a single evening in place of an old one.

Planning tips

  • Pick your top three tasks for tomorrow tonight, in order.
  • Put a 15-minute weekly review on your calendar for Sunday.
  • Plan meals for the next three days. Fewer decisions, less stress.

Self worth tips

  • Write one thing you value about yourself that has nothing to do with productivity.
  • Accept a compliment today with just "thank you." No deflecting.
  • When you compare yourself to someone today, compare with yourself a year ago instead.

Growth tips

  • Spend 10 minutes learning something just because you're curious.
  • Ask someone you trust for one piece of honest, kind feedback.

Common questions

Are these tips medical advice?

No. They are small everyday practices, educational only, and not a diagnosis or treatment. Talk to a professional about anything that worries you.

How do I choose which tip to try?

Pick the section that matches what is loudest this week, then the one tip you could do today. One tip for a few days teaches you more than ten tips read once.

Can I get a new tip each day?

Yes. A free Theraglee account shows one tip a day on your dashboard, with an affirmation, a quote and a fact beside it.

What if nothing here helps?

That is useful information, not a failure. Persistent anxiety, low mood or sleep trouble is worth taking to a licensed therapist. The Theraglee directory verifies every therapist’s license before listing them.

Educational only — not medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Find a licensed therapist if you want support.
